solutions.latex:
$$L'(t)=-\dfrac{4\pi}{365}\sin\left[\dfrac{2\pi}{365}(t+10)\right]$$

$$L''(t)=-\dfrac{8\pi^2}{365}\cos\left[\dfrac{2\pi}{365}(t+10)\right]$$

Let $L''(t)=0$

$$\begin{aligned}0&=\cos\left[\dfrac{2\pi}{365}(t+10)\right]\\\dfrac{2\pi}{365}(t+10)&=\dfrac{\pi}{2},\ \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\\t+10&=91.25,\ 273.75\\t&=81.25,\ 263.75\end{aligned}$$

$$L'(81.25)\doteq-0.03,\quad L'(263.75)\doteq0.03$$

$\therefore$ Daylight hours are increasing the fastest 264 days into the year.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct method used to find steepest gradient; 1: correctly finds first OR second derivative; 1: correct answer, clearly stating 264, not 81
review_reasons: handwritten $L''(t)$ has denominator 365 where $365^2$ is correct; does not affect the answer; kept as printed
